claim: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is the most common form of drug-resistant epilepsy in adults.
source: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is the most common form of drug-resistant epilepsy in adults and is frequently accompanied by disabling neuropsychiatric and cognitive comorbidities (Hermann et al., 2008; Hermann et al., 2000; Kwan et al., 2011; Sharma et al., 2007; Tellez-Zenteno et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: TLE is frequently accompanied by disabling neuropsychiatric and cognitive comorbidities.

evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Current anti-seizure medications are ineffective at controlling seizures in more than 30% of cases.
source: However, these treatments are ineffective at controlling seizures in more than 30% of cases (Hermann et al., 2008; Hermann et al., 2000; Kwan et al., 2011; Sharma et al., 2007; Tellez-Zenteno et al., 2007), and can cause significant adverse side effects (Alonso-Vanegas et al., 2013; Perucca and Gilliam, 2012; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Current anti-seizure medications can cause significant adverse side effects.
source: However, these treatments are ineffective at controlling seizures in more than 30% of cases (Hermann et al., 2008; Hermann et al., 2000; Kwan et al., 2011; Sharma et al., 2007; Tellez-Zenteno et al., 2007), and can cause significant adverse side effects (Alonso-Vanegas et al., 2013; Perucca and Gilliam, 2012; Taylor et al., 2011).

claim: Current ASMs are merely symptomatic and do not mitigate the severity, progression, or outcome of epilepsy.
source: Current ASMs are merely symptomatic and do not mitigate the severity, progression, or outcome of the epilepsy, and if the patient ceases the medication their seizures are just as severe and frequent as if the person has never taken the medication in the first place (Simonato et al., 2014).

claim: More than 20 new ASMs introduced to clinical practice have failed to reduce the proportion of people with drug-resistant seizures.
source: Despite decades of research and development, the more than 20 new ASMs that have been introduced to clinical practice have failed to reduce the proportion of people with epilepsy who have drug-resistant seizures (Chen et al., 2018).

claim: Cognitive and neuropsychiatric comorbidities in epilepsy patients are not improved by ASM treatment.
source: Moreover, the cognitive and neuropsychiatric comorbidities that are prevalent in these patients remain difficult to treat and are not improved by the ASM treatment (Hinnell et al., 2010; Valente and Busatto Filho, 2013).

claim: Compounds potentially capable of delaying epileptogenesis have only been demonstrated to be effective when treatment is initiated early after brain insult.
source: Animal studies have identified compounds potentially capable of delaying epileptogenesis (i.e. the process by which a non-epileptic brain turns into an epileptic one), but to date, these have only been demonstrated to be effective when the treatment is initiated early in the disease process (i.e. immediately after the brain insult) (Casillas-Espinosa et al., 2019b; Liu et al., 2016; Pauletti et al., 2019; Rizzi et al., 2019; Zeng et al., 2009; Huang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: The majority of TLE patients already have established epilepsy when they present to the clinic.
source: Because the majority of TLE patients already have established epilepsy when they present to the clinic (Foster et al., 2019), and there are no reliable biomarkers to predict who will develop TLE, this treatment strategy has limited clinical utility (Simonato et al., 2021).

claim: This is the first time a pharmacological treatment has been shown to have disease-modifying properties in chronically epileptic animals.
source:
However, the most common clinical scenario is that patients present to the clinic with established TLE, weeks to years after the epileptogenic brain insult, and in some patients, there is no identifiable brain insult (Foster et al., 2019).

The data from this study demonstrates that four weeks of sodium selenate treatment is associated with an enduring effect on mitigating the chronic epileptic state, reducing the frequency of seizures, neurocognitive, sensorimotor and neurobehavioral comorbidities, and biomarkers of disease severity. Strikingly, 4 of 12 animals (33%), did not have any seizures at all at this final timepoint eight weeks following the cessation of the treatment. In contrast, all levetiracetam and vehicle-treated animals showed spontaneous seizures at the end of the study. It is important to note that, analogous to human chronic TLE, spontaneous remission of seizures is not part of the natural history of the post-KA SE rat model of chronic TLE (Van Nieuwenhuyse et al., 2015a; Williams et al., 2009).

Behavioral comorbidities are considered an integral part of the TLE disease (Brooks-Kayal et al., 2013; Mazarati et al., 2018). Patients with chronic and drug-resistant TLE have an increased prevalence of psychiatric conditions, memory, and learning disabilities (Kandratavicius et al., 2012; Ott et al., 2003; Stafstrom et al., 1993; Stores, 1971; Tellez-Zenteno et al., 2007). Cognitive impairment is the most common comorbidity that afflicts people with TLE and tends to resist treatment, even after epilepsy surgery (Hermann et al., 2000). In fact, in a proportion of cases, the cognitive dysfunction progresses despite successful seizure control (Amlerova et al., 2014; Berg et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2014; Taylor et al., 2010). In keeping with the human condition, cognitive deficits have been demonstrated as a comorbidity in the post-SE animal model (Detour et al., 2005; Pearson et al., 2014; Chauvière et al., 2009). Here, we found that animals treated with sodium selenate had improved spatial memory and recognition memory, comparable to non-epileptic controls. This is the first time that a treatment has been described to reverse memory deficits in established chronic TLE.
evidence: Based on the novelty of the findings in the context of existing literature

evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Sensorimotor deficits in TLE are not necessarily associated with the presence of seizures or with the use of ASMs.
source: Sensorimotor deficits are another significant comorbidity in people with TLE (Girardi-Schappo et al., 2021; Gandelman-Marton et al., 2006), and are not necessarily associated with the presence of seizures or with the use of ASMs (Gandelman-Marton et al., 2006; Petty et al., 2010; Shiek Ahmad et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Patients with drug-resistant TLE have abnormal postural instability and an increased risk of falls compared to healthy controls.
source: A study in patients with drug-resistant TLE found abnormal postural instability and an increased risk of falls than healthy controls (Gandelman-Marton et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Transgenic mouse models that expressed hyperphosphorylated tau present cognitive dysfunction and sensorimotor impairments.
source: Interestingly, transgenic mouse models that expressed h-tau have been described to not only present cognitive dysfunction but also sensorimotor impairments (Kreilaus et al., 2021; Leroy et al., 2007; Lewis et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Sodium selenate treatment mitigated sensorimotor deficits in chronically epileptic rats in the post-KA SE model of TLE.
source: Here, we found that sodium selenate treatment mitigated the sensorimotor deficits in chronically epileptic rats in the post-KA SE model of TLE.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the beam task

claim: Pathological hyperphosphorylated tau is a key pathophysiological driver of drug-resistant TLE and associated comorbidities.
source: The results from this study add to the growing literature that indicates that pathological h-tau is a key pathophysiological driver of drug-resistant TLE and associated comorbidities.
evidence: Based on the findings of this study and existing literature

claim: The persistent disease-modifying effects of sodium selenate in drug-resistant TLE correlate to increased expression of the B catalytic subunit of PP2A and reduction of hyperphosphorylated tau.
source: Our data indicate that the persistent disease-modifying effects of sodium selenate in drug-resistant TLE correlate to the increased the expression of the B catalytic subunit of PP2A and the reduction of h-tau.
evidence: Supported by proteomic and western blot data from this study

claim: The PP2A B subunit is specifically involved in the dephosphorylation of tau.
source: Evidence has shown that the PP2A B subunit is specifically involved in the dephosphorylation of tau (Barnes et al., 1995; Corcoran et al., 2010a) and PP2A expression and activity are potentiated by sodium selenate (Corcoran et al., 2010a; Jones et al., 2012; Shultz et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: PP2A expression and activity are potentiated by sodium selenate.
source: Evidence has shown that the PP2A B subunit is specifically involved in the dephosphorylation of tau (Barnes et al., 1995; Corcoran et al., 2010a) and PP2A expression and activity are potentiated by sodium selenate (Corcoran et al., 2010a; Jones et al., 2012; Shultz et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: In resected tissue from patients with drug-resistant TLE, PP2A protein expression is significantly decreased.
source: In resected tissue from patients with drug-resistant TLE, PP2A protein expression is also significantly decreased, but remains unchanged in Alzheimer's disease patients, indicating that PP2A alterations may be an epilepsy-specific pathology (Gourmaud et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: PP2A alterations may be an epilepsy-specific pathology.
source: In resected tissue from patients with drug-resistant TLE, PP2A protein expression is also significantly decreased, but remains unchanged in Alzheimer's disease patients, indicating that PP2A alterations may be an epilepsy-specific pathology (Gourmaud et al., 2020).
evidence: Inferred from comparison between TLE and Alzheimer's disease patients, supported by citation

claim: Tau-based mechanisms enhance neuronal excitability.
source: There is also building evidence that tau-based mechanisms enhance neuronal excitability.
evidence: Based on existing literature

claim: Alterations in tau phosphorylation have been implicated in changing the excitation/inhibition balance in neurons.
source: Alterations in tau phosphorylation have been implicated in changing the excitation/inhibition balance in the neurons (Palop et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Unstable microtubule assembly at axonal segments, as seen with the presence of hyperphosphorylated tau, dysregulates the resting membrane potential and generation of action potentials.
source: Unstable microtubule assembly at axonal segments, as seen with the presence of h-tau, dysregulates the resting membrane potential and thereby generations of action potentials (Matsumoto and Sakai, 1979).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Tau is transported into the cell via Fyn kinase where it influences N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-mediated excitotoxicity.
source: Tau is transported into the cell via Fyn kinase where it influences N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-mediated excitotoxicity (van Eersel et al., 2010) and changes in tau has been correlated with dysfunction of axonal NMDA receptors which are all considered mechanisms that promote the expression of seizures (Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: Changes in tau have been correlated with dysfunction of axonal NMDA receptors which are mechanisms that promote the expression of seizures.
source: Tau is transported into the cell via Fyn kinase where it influences N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-mediated excitotoxicity (van Eersel et al., 2010) and changes in tau has been correlated with dysfunction of axonal NMDA receptors which are all considered mechanisms that promote the expression of seizures (Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Pathological hyperphosphorylated tau has been proposed as one of the main culprits underlying cognitive deficits across different neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, TBI, and epilepsy.
source: Pathological h-tau, has been proposed as one of the main culprits underlying cognitive deficits across different neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, TBI, and epilepsy (Casillas-Espinosa et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Accumulation of hyperphosphorylated tau in temporal lobe brain tissue from patients with drug-resistant TLE is associated with cognitive decline.
source: Accumulation of h-tau in temporal lobe brain tissue from patients with drug-resistant TLE is associated with cognitive decline (Gourmaud et al., 2020; Thom et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: Tau pathology has been associated with a decline in verbal learning, recall, and graded naming test scores in different neurodegenerative disorders.
source: Furthermore, tau pathology has been associated with a decline in verbal learning, recall, and graded naming test scores in different neurodegenerative disorders (Tai et al., 2016) and in animal models that overexpressed h-tau (Kreilaus et al., 2021; Leroy et al., 2007; Lewis et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: For some animals, the effects of sodium selenate were only observed several weeks after cessation of treatment, and the magnitude of the decrease in seizure expression progressively increased over the eight weeks of follow-up post-treatment.
source: It is interesting that for some of the animals, the effects of sodium selenate were only observed several weeks after cessation of treatment, and the magnitude of the decrease in seizure expression progressively increased over the eight weeks of follow-up post-treatment.
evidence: Supported by experimental observation from seizure data

claim: Spontaneous remission of seizures is not part of the natural history of the post-KA SE rat model of chronic TLE.
source: It is important to note that, analogous to human chronic TLE, spontaneous remission of seizures is not part of the natural history of the post-KA SE rat model of chronic TLE (Van Nieuwenhuyse et al., 2015a; Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: Cognitive impairment is the most common comorbidity that afflicts people with TLE and tends to resist treatment, even after epilepsy surgery.
source: Cognitive impairment is the most common comorbidity that afflicts people with TLE and tends to resist treatment, even after epilepsy surgery (Hermann et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: In a proportion of TLE cases, cognitive dysfunction progresses despite successful seizure control.
source: In fact, in a proportion of cases, the cognitive dysfunction progresses despite successful seizure control (Amlerova et al., 2014; Berg et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2014; Taylor et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Cognitive deficits have been demonstrated as a comorbidity in the post-SE animal model.
source: In keeping with the human condition, cognitive deficits have been demonstrated as a comorbidity in the post-SE animal model (Detour et al., 2005; Pearson et al., 2014; Chauvière et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: There is significant upregulation of IGFR1 and FGFR signaling cascades and FGFR-mediated PI-3K cascade activation in the selenate-treated group compared to vehicle.
source: Based on the PADOG analysis results, there is significant upregulation of IGFR1 and FGFR signaling cascades and FGFR-mediated PI-3K cascade activation in the selenate-treated group compared to the vehicle.
evidence: Supported by pathway enrichment analysis of proteomic data

claim: The downregulation of fatty acid oxidation processes in the selenate group suggests a shift from hyperactive neurons with high-energy demand towards neurons with lower energy demand.
source: The downregulation of fatty acid oxidation processes in the selenate group suggests a shift from hyperactive neurons with high-energy demand (like in epileptic seizures) towards neurons with lower energy demand.
evidence: Inferred from pathway analysis results

claim: This analysis is the first attempt at the integration of metabolomic and proteomic data in an epilepsy network medicine paradigm.
source: To our knowledge, this analysis is the first attempt at the integration of metabolomic and proteomic data in an epilepsy network medicine paradigm.
evidence: Based on the novelty of the approach in the context of epilepsy research

claim: Multi-omic, data-driven correlation networks can be used for agnostic, hypothesis-free examination of disease states and identification of specific protein-metabolite modules associated with different states and treatments.
source: We demonstrate that multi-omic, data-driven correlation networks can be used for agnostic, hypothesis-free examination of disease states as well as the identification of specific protein-metabolite modules associated with different states and treatments.
evidence: Based on the network analysis performed in this study

claim: No prognostic biomarkers for TLE currently exist.
source: Prognostic biomarkers are used to predict disease characteristics and identify disease recurrence or progression in patients who have the disease of interest. Unfortunately, no such prognostic biomarkers for TLE currently exist (Simonato et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Telomere length has emerged as a potential prognostic biomarker of chronic neurodegenerative conditions.
source: Telomere length has emerged as a potential prognostic biomarker of chronic neurodegenerative conditions (Chan et al., 2020; Kang et al., 2020; Galletly et al., 2017; Lukens et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Telomeres are repetitive non-coding DNA-tandem sequences of TTAGGG found at the end of eukaryotic chromosomes.
source: Telomeres are repetitive non-coding DNA-tandem sequences of TTAGGG found at the end of eukaryotic chromosomes (Hehar and Mychasiuk, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: Telomere length has been used as a biological marker for cellular aging and has been described in many neurological disorders.
source: Telomere length has been used as a biological marker for cellular aging and has been described in many neurological disorders (Hehar and Mychasiuk, 2016; Koppelstaetter et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2019; Wright et al., 2018), including TLE (Miranda et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Telomere length has been described in TLE.
source: Telomere length has been used as a biological marker for cellular aging and has been described in many neurological disorders (Hehar and Mychasiuk, 2016; Koppelstaetter et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2019; Wright et al., 2018), including TLE (Miranda et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: There is a strong correlation between telomere length in the brain and peripheral skin cells.
source: Here, we analyzed telomere length from ear biopsies, as previous evidence has shown a strong correlation between telomere length in the brain and peripheral skin cells (Hehar and Mychasiuk, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature

claim: The magnitude of reduced telomere length was strongly associated with the number of seizures and more pronounced cognitive deficits in the drug-resistant TLE model.
source: The magnitude of the reduced telomere length was strongly associated with the number of seizures and more pronounced cognitive deficits in our drug-resistant TLE model.
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of experimental data

claim: Telomere length has potential as a prognostic biomarker of disease severity, treatment response, and TLE disease modification.
source: Overall, our data highlights the potential of telomere length as a prognostic biomarker of disease severity, treatment response, and TLE disease modification, which has the potential to be used in further trials of DMT.
evidence: Based on the findings of this study

claim: Pathway/network-based prognostic markers should be inherently more reliable than individual markers since they provide biological interpretation for the association between multiple molecules and disease characteristics.
source: Unlike individual markers, pathway/network-based prognostic markers should be inherently more reliable since they provide the biological interpretation for the association between multiple molecules and the disease characteristics (seizures, behavior comorbidities, development of TLE) (Zou et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature and logical reasoning

claim: Sodium selenate treatment for four weeks has disease-modifying effects in an animal model of chronic drug-resistant TLE.
source: This study reports novel data that demonstrates that sodium selenate treatment for four weeks has disease-modifying effects in an animal model of chronic drug-resistant TLE.
evidence: Supported by the experimental data from this study

claim: Sodium selenate has been shown to be safe and well tolerated in early-phase clinical trials for other conditions.
source: This approach is highly translatable, given that sodium selenate has already been shown to be safe and well tolerated in early-phase clinical trials for other conditions (Cardoso et al., 2019; Corcoran et al., 2010b; Malpas et al., 2016; Vivash et al., 2020), and there are a large number of patients with chronic drug-resistant TLE.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published literature

claim: Post-SE animals treated with vehicle had a reduced sucrose preference compared to shams.
source: Analysis of the 24 hr sucrose preference test (SPT) showed that post-SE animals treated with vehicle had a reduced preference for the 2% sucrose solution when compared to shams (p<0.05, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Reduced sucrose preference can be interpreted as anhedonia, one of the major diagnostic criteria of depressive-like disorders in humans.
source: Reduced sucrose preference can be interpreted as anhedonia, one of the major diagnostic criteria of depressive-like disorders in humans (Casillas-Espinosa et al., 2019b; Jones et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature

claim: Sucrose preference was not significantly different between selenate, levetiracetam, and shams.
source: Sucrose preference was not significantly different between selenate, levetiracetam, and shams.
evidence: Supported by experimental observation
